candidates.old:
LDY act_n
    BEQ taken_off
.taking_off
    DEY
    STY ren_k
    LDX act,Y
    BEQ taken_off                   \ the player: first in the list, already off
candidates.new:
LDY act_n
    BNE taking_off                  \ grind: the loop below tests need before calling take_off, as put_on's loop does
    BRA taken_off                   \ nothing listed
.tko_first                          \ index 0 (Y = 0): the player first in the list, already off; else a mover
    LDX act
    BEQ taken_off                   \ the player
    LDA need,X
    BPL taken_off                   \ take_off's own first test: nothing to take off
    BRA tko_call
.taking_off
    DEY
    BEQ tko_first                   \ the entry just taken was index 1: index 0 is the one left
    LDX act,Y                       \ index 1 and up: never the player (slot 0 is first in the list when listed)
    LDA need,X
    BPL taking_off                  \ take_off's own first test (bit 7: take off): nothing to do, next
.tko_call
    STY ren_k
candidates.summary: take_off loop (step 4): test need bit 7 inline (as put_on's loop already does) and skip the JSR take_off whose whole job would be LDA need,X / BPL out / RTS; index 0 is split out so the DEY's Z flag is both the loop end and the old player test. 15 cycles a skipped entry instead of 36. ALTERNATIVE to the second candidate (overlaps lines 479-485) and the better of the two: +17 bytes, but they land every later hot branch where it did not cross a page (estimated penalty about 0, against +7.7 for the 6-byte one).
candidates.equivalence: Measured on the bench build (ctl-3db31c8, pcprof with a hook at take_off): the loop calls take_off 5.9 times a pass on seed 1 (1.32 of them with need bit 7 set) and 6.6 on RIGHT (1.08 set), so 4.6 and 5.5 entries a pass are skips. take_off for a slot with bit 7 clear is exactly LDA need,X / BPL out / RTS: no store, X and Y untouched, A and flags dead. So skipping it changes nothing but A, flags (dead: the tail reloads Y from ren_k and the loop top overwrites X and A) and ren_k, which a skip no longer writes. ren_k is read in render.6502 only at 487 (the tail, after our STY ren_k), 509 (after STY ren_k at 499) and 1039/1072/1087 (mark_to_draw, close_over_overlaps, after their own STY ren_k at 1011/1060): nothing reads what the loop used to leave. Liveness at .taken_off (build/annotated): in:- (A, X, Y, flags all dead). Control flow: act_n = 0 -> taken_off (BNE not taken, BRA). act_n >= 1 -> taking_off: DEY; Y = 0 -> tko_first: act[0] is the player (X = 0: the original BEQ taken_off at index 0) or another slot. act is written only by classify (X ascending, so slot 0 can only be at index 0 and every index >= 1 has X >= 1: the original BEQ taken_off at 485 can fire only at index 0). A non-player at index 0 with bit 7 clear: the original called take_off (no-op), LDY ren_k = 0, BNE not taken -> taken_off; ours goes to taken_off. With bit 7 set: BRA tko_call, STY ren_k (Y = 0), the tail's JSR take_off, LDY ren_k = 0, BNE falls out to taken_off: identical. Y >= 1: X = act[Y], bit 7 clear -> BPL taking_off with Y = index and the next DEY gives index - 1, as the original tail's LDY ren_k did; bit 7 set -> falls into tko_call: STY ren_k, JSR take_off, LDY ren_k (= index >= 1), BNE taking_off: the original's path. take_off is called on exactly the same slots in the same order (last listed first, then index 0 if not the player). The first call (LDX #0 / JSR take_off, lines 477-478) is untouched. DEBUG_FULLREDRAW and SKY_MODE builds: take_off's first two instructions are the same in every build.
candidates.relies_on: Pages (bench build, bank 4, DATA1; addresses from tools/grind.read_dbg and the ssd's bytes): the window's code starts at &92D9 (line 479) and the tail (JSR take_off / LDY ren_k / BNE taking_off, lines 486-488, unchanged) is the next line after the window, reached by fall-through. Shift +17 bytes for everything in bank 4 after the window (render_end has 797 bytes free; ASSERT render_end <= REN_BASE). All of the new loop stays inside page &92 (tko_first &92DF, taking_off &92EA, BPL &92F2, tko_call &92F4, tail BNE &92FB), so none of its taken branches crosses. Branch crossings moved by +17, measured over every hot branch after the window and weighted by heat/2.6 (conditional) or heat/3 (BRA): BRA gather (14.0 cycles heat), BEQ no_part (7.6) and BNE whole_pages (8.4) go into a crossing, BNE shown (19.6) and BEQ scrolled (2.5) come out of one: net estimate -0.6 cycles. The same estimate for +6 bytes is +7.7 and for +11 it is +32 (BPL fast_row would cross), so do not trim this candidate by a byte or two without recounting. Relies on slot 0 only ever being first in act (classify is the only writer; mark_to_draw and close_over_overlaps only read it). Tables read by indexed loads after the window (lives_digits,Y at &9444, straight_sprite_*, sprite_column_count, ck_*, wa_rows_*) move with the shift; whether any starts to cross depends on index range and was not checked: the gate will say. No label or entry past a label is touched: taking_off and taken_off are referenced only inside src/render.6502 (grep over src/ and tools/ finds no other use, and no existing tko_ label); ren_k and need are zero page (&4E, &1F+), written by nobody but render.6502.

LDY act_n
    BEQ taken_off
.taking_off
    DEY
    BMI taken_off                   \ grind: Y was 0, index 0 was a skip and the list is done
    LDX act,Y
    BEQ taken_off                   \ the player: first in the list, already off
    LDA need,X
    BPL taking_off                  \ take_off's own first test (bit 7: take off): nothing to do, next
    STY ren_k
candidates.summary: Same skip of take_off for entries with need bit 7 clear (17 cycles a skipped entry instead of 36), smaller: only +6 bytes, the DEY running past index 0 to $FF is the end test (BMI). ALTERNATIVE to the first candidate (overlaps lines 479-485); 2 cycles a skipped entry slower, and +6 bytes pushes BNE going_on, BRA gather and BEQ no_part (close_over_overlaps) across a page for an estimated +7.7 cycles a pass.
candidates.equivalence: As the first candidate: take_off for a slot whose need bit 7 is clear is LDA need,X / BPL out / RTS with no side effect, so skipping it is invisible (A and flags dead at the loop top and at taken_off; ren_k not written on a skip and never read before being written again, see the first candidate). Control flow: act_n = 0 -> taken_off as before. Otherwise Y = count; DEY gives the index; Y = $FF (the previous index was 0, skipped as non-stale: BPL taking_off was taken from index 0) -> BMI taken_off, the end of the list (original: LDY ren_k = 0, BNE falls out); otherwise X = act[Y]; X = 0 -> taken_off (the player: only at index 0, as in the original); bit 7 clear -> BPL taking_off with Y = index, and the DEY there gives index - 1, as the original tail's LDY ren_k did; bit 7 set -> STY ren_k then the unchanged tail: JSR take_off, LDY ren_k, BNE taking_off (index 0 stale: ren_k = 0, falls out to taken_off as in the original). The BMI is reached only through the BPL from index 0 (Y goes 0 -> $FF); at index 0 with the player BEQ taken_off comes first; at entry Y >= 1 so the first DEY never gives $FF.
